surfaces.part: cobble field (rounded cobbles with dark joints, seen from above)
dressed stone kerb rim, north and side edges (light top strip, 2 rows)
dressed stone kerb, south edge front face (2 rows) with a cast shadow on the grass below

answer.evidence: This is a flat ground autotile sheet. Each cobbled patch is a top-down field of cobbles that fills nearly the whole patch, for example rows 20-57 in the top-left block. The kerb is a light 1-2 row rim on the north and side edges (rows 18-19 at x=48). On the south edge it has only a 2-row front face (light stone row then a dark joint or shadow row), followed by 1-2 rows of shadow on the grass. That is fewer than 3 front-face rows, and no vertical body or receding side face is drawn. The tile is therefore a flat slab, which is normal for terrain, rather than a standing object with a top and a front.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 4 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 7 for the paving reference and 3 for the grass. Near-flat coverage is 7%, so the surface is not flat, and the cobbles carry some variation. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans warm brown and reads as a dark material tone, not a sticker line. The cobbles are small round dots in a few warm tones with dark joints, and each cobble has only about 2-3 steps (highlight, body, shadow). The stone kerb is a pale beige band with little per-stone shading, and the 2px south face is barely distinguishable from the rim. The grass base is a repeating tuft pattern in a narrow green range. It looks tiled and flatter than the Beodeul grass with its clumps and darker patches. The piece is cleanly built but has fewer shading steps than the 5-6 per material in the references, so it is a bit shallow.

surfaces.part: dressed stone kerb rim with 2px south front face

answer.evidence: The sheet is a flat autotile layout of cobble ground on grass. The cobble field is seen from directly above (round stones and dark joints), with no foreshortened raised top. The only vertical face is the thin 2-row kerb on the south edges (light rim at rows 18-19 in the column scans, then a dark joint row), which is under the 3-row minimum for a front face. The shape is a ground slab with a rim, not a standing volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The cobbles are readable as individual stones: warm brown and grey stones with a tan highlight dot on a dark earth joint. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is a material tone, not a black sticker line. Each stone has only about 3 steps (joint, mid, highlight), and the kerb rim is a thin pale band with little per-stone shading. The grass is a faint repeating tuft pattern in 2-3 close greens. The measured 4 visible tones per tile and 4 raw colours per tile are well below the paving reference (7 visible tones). They are only level with the grass reference (3), and the rest of the candidate is cobbles. Raw colour count per tile is not the deciding fact. The shading ramps are still clearly shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material, and the cobble field is uniformly dense but thin in tone variety. When in doubt, fail.
